name: Borage

schedule.notes: Taproot — doesn't transplant well. Plant once; it self-seeds reliably from then on.
Pick flowers daily for salads; leaves while young.

harvest.cues: Star-shaped blue flowers fully open. Young leaves 2 to 4 in, still tender.
harvest.storageNotes: Flowers wilt within hours — eat the day picked. Leaves don't store well.

varieties.name: White Borage
varieties.notes: White flowers, less common, equally vigorous.

notes: Flowers taste like cucumber — beautiful frozen into ice cubes for summer drinks. Plant next to tomatoes and strawberries; alleged to deter hornworms and improve fruit set. Hairy leaves are an acquired texture; flowers are the prize.
